previous_last_sync.summary: Anti-lag now requires a valid driver throttle-intent signal before it can arm, and the anti-lag ETB target addition is applied only when anti-lag is enabled and the accelerator-pedal reading is valid. The ETB pedal-target page is updated to describe these conditions.

decisions.rationale: Anti-lag arming now fails closed: if the driver throttle-intent signal is missing or non-finite, the anti-lag throttle condition is false and anti-lag does not activate, even if RPM, coolant, and switch conditions are met. The anti-lag ETB target addition is also gated on anti-lag being enabled and on a valid, finite accelerator-pedal reading, so a stale active flag or a failed pedal sensor no longer adds ALSEtbAdd to the throttle target. No tune migration is required; existing anti-lag tunes keep their settings. Check that the pedal and throttle-intent sensors are calibrated and healthy before relying on anti-lag, and treat a lost pedal signal as an anti-lag inhibit rather than a fault to tune around.
evidence: firmware/controllers/algo/antilag_system.cpp: isALSMaxThrottleIntentCondition now returns false when Sensor::get(SensorType::DriverThrottleIntent) is invalid or non-finite
firmware/controllers/actuators/electronic_throttle.cpp: getSetpointEtbNonTorqueModel adds ALSEtbAdd only if antiLagEnabled and isAntilagCondition and the AcceleratorPedal reading is valid and finite
unit_tests/tests/actuators/test_antilag.cpp: new AntiLagRequiresValidThrottleIntent test covers invalid, NaN, recovery, and re-arm
unit_tests/tests/actuators/test_etb.cpp: new antiLagAdderRequiresEnabledAndValidPedal test covers stale flag, invalid pedal, and disabled anti-lag

last_sync.summary: Capoworks ECU now applies the anti-lag soft spark-skip ratio only while anti-lag is both enabled and actively engaged. Previously the configured skip ratio could suppress sparks whenever the limiter was evaluated, even with anti-lag disabled or not armed. The change is a firmware behavior fix with unit-test coverage; no tune migration is required, but anti-lag spark skipping should be re-verified on the bench.

decisions.rationale: Capoworks ECU changed anti-lag soft spark skipping so the configured ALSSkipRatio is applied only when anti-lag is enabled and the anti-lag controller reports an active condition; otherwise the target skip ratio is zero. Drivers and tuners no longer lose sparks to a stale skip ratio when anti-lag is off or not armed, and skipping resumes when anti-lag re-arms. No tune migration is needed, but re-check anti-lag spark behavior on the bench because the change is validated only by unit tests, not on an engine.
evidence: firmware/controllers/engine_cycle/spark_logic.cpp: ALSSkipRatio now computed as antiLagEnabled && antilagController.isAntilagCondition ? ALSSkipRatio : 0.0f and applied via ALSsoftSparkLimiter.setTargetSkipRatio() at the top of onTriggerEventSparkLogic
firmware/controllers/engine_cycle/spark_logic.cpp: removed the unconditional setTargetSkipRatio(engineConfiguration->ALSSkipRatio) call from the per-event scheduling loop
